# issue: 3429
# what: characterising the agent `grep` tool's false-zero behaviour under `.github/`.
# why:  this is a tooling defect that silently confirms whatever the worker hoped to confirm.
#       Raised by the batch-009 orchestrator, who measured `grep` finding ZERO files
#       containing `dxc-issue-triage` under `.github/` where `Select-String` finds 15.
#       I had recorded a narrower (and wrong) diagnosis: "it only fails on single-file paths".
#       Neither framing is right. Measured below.
#
# All queries below are rooted at:
#   <triage>/data/issues/3429
# `.github` is a hidden directory; ripgrep skips hidden paths unless told otherwise.

==============================================================================
GROUND TRUTH (PowerShell Select-String, which does not skip hidden paths)

  Select-String -Path *.* -Pattern 'TGSM'  -List   ->  61 files
  Select-String -Path *.* -Pattern 'audit' -List   ->   1 file  (method-notes.md)

==============================================================================
GREP WITHOUT A `glob` FILTER  --  ALL FALSE ZEROS

  grep 'audit'            paths=<dir>            ->  No matches found     WRONG (truth: 1)
  grep 'TGSM'             paths=<dir>            ->  No matches found     WRONG (truth: 61)
  grep 'audit'            paths=<method-notes.md> ->  No matches found    WRONG (truth: 1)
  grep 'ever compiled|no shipped release'
                          paths=<dir>            ->  No matches found     WRONG (was in 2 files)

  3 of these were directory queries and 1 was a single-file query, so the defect is NOT
  specific to single-file paths -- my earlier note said it was, and that was wrong.

==============================================================================
GREP WITH A `glob` FILTER  --  ACCURATE IN EVERY CASE

  grep 'audit'                 glob=*.md   ->  1 file: method-notes.md
                                               matches Select-String exactly (1)

  grep '^## |audit|self-check' glob=*.md   ->  24 matches across 3 files
                                               (this is the one query of mine that worked,
                                                and it is the one that carried a glob)

  grep 'TGSM'                  glob=*.txt  ->  105 matches across 49 files
                                               Select-String reports 61 files across ALL
                                               extensions, of which the .txt subset is 49.
                                               Consistent.

==============================================================================
# CONCLUSION
#
# The trigger is the ABSENCE of a `glob` filter, not the path shape:
#
#   grep under .github/ WITHOUT glob  ->  false zero            (4 of 4 observations)
#   grep under .github/ WITH    glob  ->  correct results       (3 of 3 observations)
#
# This is more precise than "do not use grep under .github/": grep is usable there, but ONLY
# with a glob. It is also more dangerous than a plain outage, because the failure mode is a
# clean "No matches found" with no error -- indistinguishable from a true negative.
#
# Rule adopted: whenever a ZERO result is the meaningful answer (e.g. "have I removed that
# claim from my write-up?"), verify with Select-String, which has no hidden-path behaviour:
#
#   Select-String -Path data\issues\<n>\*.md -Pattern 'claim text'
#
# `glob` (the separate tool) is unaffected -- it lists files under .github/ correctly.
